title: Elastic throughput bands prototype
content:
Quick framing / goal:
- Want a simple mechanism that (a) maps customer commit+burst into predictable unit economics and (b) makes it easy for product to explain performance buckets (latency/throughput) without complex custom SKUs.
- Keep mostly PAYG semantics for small customers; introduce 'throughput bands' for mid-size customers as a cheap-to-explain middle ground between pure PAYG and Reserved Dedicated.

Idea: Elastic throughput bands (ETB)
- Customer chooses a band: e.g. 10rps, 50rps, 200rps (rps = sustained request slots at 16k context)
- Each band has a committed monthly token allowance (tokens/mo) derived from expected tokens per request and concurrency shape. Burst pool for short-term >band usage.
- Billing = base monthly fee (band commit) + payg tokens beyond commit + burst overage if burst pool exceeded.

Why this helps:
- Translates GPU-backed throughput commitments into an easy customer concept (requests/second).
- For us: allows predictable packing and binning on serving clusters, simplifies autoscaling planning.
- For customers: simpler than token quotas but more flexible than long-term reserved capacity.

Back-of-envelope unit math (prototype numbers)
Assumptions:
- Model A (latency-optimized gen) cost to serve = $1.20 / GPU-hour effective after infra overheads (amortized across many tenants) — placeholder, confirm with infra.
- Average tokens per request: 1,200 tokens (input + output combined) for typical chat exchange in mid-tier app.
- Effective token throughput per GPU-hour at production batching/kv-cache = 12M tokens/hour (derived from internal perf tests).

Therefore unit cost per token = $1.20 / 12,000,000 = $0.0000001 per token (1e-7) => $0.0001 per 1k tokens.
Multiply up for safety margin: use $0.00015 per 1k tokens (includes ops overhead + margin).

Map to requests: average cost per request = 1,200 tokens * $0.00000015 = $0.00018/request.
So 10 rps sustained -> 10 * 3600 * 24 * 30 = 25,920,000 requests/month -> that seems huge; oops check: 10 rps * seconds per month (2,592,000) = 25,920,000 requests.
Monthly tokens = 25.92M requests * 1,200 tokens = 31.1B tokens/mo.
Token cost raw = 31.1B tokens / 1000 * $0.00015 = $4,665/mo.
(This aligns to dedicated-like economics, which is expected at higher sustained rps.)

Example band pricing (sketch):
- Band S: 10 rps commit -> base fee $5,500/mo includes 31B tokens, burst pool 10B tokens, overage $0.00020/1k tokens
- Band M: 50 rps commit -> base fee $24,000/mo includes 155B tokens, burst pool 40B tokens, overage $0.00018/1k
- Band L: 200 rps commit -> base fee $88,000/mo includes 620B tokens, burst pool 200B tokens, overage $0.00015/1k
Notes: all numbers rough; band price = (estimated infra cost + ops margin + SLA premium + amortized idle cushion).

Burst mechanics (practical heuristics)
- Short bursts up to X% of committed rate for T minutes draw from burst pool. Burst pool size = committed_tokens * burst_multiplier (e.g., 0.3 for small band).
- If burst pool exhausted, throttle or route to cheaper model variant (see fallback below).
- Implement per-minute reconciliation and reporting in console.

Cheaper fallback model variant & graceful degradation
- Offer automatic fallback to quantized variant (Model A-q8) with slightly higher hallucination risk but lower cost (cost multiplier 0.45).
- Policy: if sustained 1m throughput exceeds band by >50% and burst pool exhausted, route a sample of traffic to A-q8 (10% initially) and expand if quality checks pass.
- Can be a configurable tenant-level knob in console.

Session vs token semantics trade-offs
- Session-bundles are friendlier to UX teams (predictability) but hard when token variance is high (long user messages).
- Band approach lets us keep token accounting under the hood and expose rps + estimated monthly usage to customer.
- Consider hybrid offering: band commit + optional session-bundle add-on for deterministic conversational UX (e.g., 1,000 sessions/mo included).

Edge cases / open questions (to follow up)
- How to normalize token counts across models with different context lengths and kv-cache reuse? (we likely need normalized token units per model: e.g., normalized_tokens = raw_tokens * model_multiplier).
- Do we charge for request metadata / attachments differently (images, tool calls)?
- How to handle idle reserved capacity when customers underutilize for long windows? Offer cross-tenant pooling or roll-over credits?
- Taxonomy: map metric names to console UI ("band", "sustained rps", "burst pool", "normalized tokens").
- Legal/contract: minimum commit length (30d vs 90d) and early-termination handling.

Quick sensitivity checks (very rough)
- If we under-estimate token throughput per GPU-hour by 25%, the base fee should increase ~33% to keep margin. That suggests conservative multipliers when mapping perf tests to pricing.
- If customers actually average 600 tokens/request rather than 1,200, Band S economics cut in half — need example profiles (mobile bot vs longform assistant).

Implementation roadmap (MVP)
1) Define 3 bands (S/M/L) with default commit -> engineering provides packing plans and expected utilization curves.
2) Console: show projected monthly tokens, burst pool, and traffic meter in real-time.
3) Billing: support base fee + PAYG token overage and burst accounting.
4) Policy: default fallback to Model A-q8 with opt-out.

Next steps / TODOs
- Ask infra for updated GPU-hour effective token throughput (ticket INFRA-872).
- Run quick sims with 20 customer profiles from Growth cohort (ticket PRICING-312).
- Draft wording for sales one-pager and new pricing FAQ.

Random scratch notes:
- Might be simpler to express bands in 'tokens per minute' instead of rps since token-based thinking is more accurate for nonuniform responses.
- Pricing names: keep neutral (Band S/M/L) or pick product-y names (Starter, Scale, Enterprise) depending on GTM tempo.
- Keep a clear table in console: projected bill if you exceed commit by 10/25/50% (helps sales).

End of notes.
